findings.summary: Proposal Apply reused the public proposal UUID as the command-batch idempotency key, allowing a direct caller to pre-consume that UUID and interfere with Apply semantics.
findings.repair: Proposal Apply now creates a server-owned UUID inside the same transaction and records it only as safe audit metadata; the proposal remains the terminal Apply identity.

findings.summary: Child rows had independent tenant_id and session_id foreign keys, so the database did not structurally prove that a child tenant matched its session tenant; broad default table privileges also required explicit narrowing.
findings.repair: Sessions now expose UNIQUE(id, tenant_id); versions/events/proposals use composite session+tenant foreign keys; runtime DELETE/immutable UPDATE privileges are explicitly revoked; proposal content and terminal transitions are DB-enforced.

findings.summary: Canonical set/key ordering used localeCompare, which can depend on ICU/locale and is not an appropriate content-addressing primitive.
findings.repair: Canonical ordering now uses locale-independent lexical code-unit comparison for object keys, sponsor refs and every set-like state/command array.

findings.summary: SET_SPONSOR_SCOPE command parsing validated shape but not sponsor cardinality/coalition semantics, so a proposal that could never Apply could be persisted.
findings.repair: Semantic sponsor invariants now live in the strict command schema before normalization/persistence while duplicate identical client refs remain normalizable.

findings.summary: Criteria/ref command strings were bounded but did not uniformly reject disallowed control characters.
findings.repair: Controlled text/ref schemas now share the control-character rejection contract used by Campaign Spec text.

findings.summary: A proposal proactively superseded by a successful state mutation later returned OUTREACH_PROPOSAL_ALREADY_DECIDED on Apply rather than the deterministic stale-proposal conflict.
findings.repair: Apply maps terminal superseded proposals to OUTREACH_PROPOSAL_STALE with the current state version while retaining eager supersession.

findings.summary: The command registry labelled implemented/future commands but did not mechanically enforce implemented=>reducer and future=>no reducer authority.
findings.repair: Registry entries now carry parser/reducer authority and boot validation rejects implemented commands without a reducer or future commands with one.

findings.summary: The ordered-upgrade DB rehearsal seeded identity rows once for the legacy sentinel and again for database invariants, causing the harness to fail on its own duplicate fixture.
findings.repair: Disposable identity fixture creation is idempotent by primary key.

notes: No finding was closed by weakening an acceptance assertion.
No shared database migration, deployment, feature-flag enablement, canonical cutover, or external action has been performed.
The focused Prisma projection exists because Phase 2 state locking uses explicit SQL; DB-only invariants are pinned by static and disposable-Postgres gates.
Browser acceptance remains deployed-app based per owner direction; no localhost Clerk/browser result will be relabelled as passing.
